purpose: Teach: 高音/逸話/吸引/教区/脱皮/表層/平原/氷河

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、楽器の高音域研究を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, you wrote your paper on high-frequency sounds in musical instruments, didn't you?
lines.style: Warm, observational opening. Gentle confirmation rather than question. Steady, encouraging eye contact. The tone of a teacher checking in she already knows the answer.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、歴史人物の逸話研究を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes, I wrote mine on historical anecdotes about important figures.
lines.style: Quiet, genuine response. Light hesitation at the start—gathering his thoughts before committing. Even pace, no embellishment. The honesty of someone who means exactly what he says.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、医療機器の吸引技術を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: And your paper covered suction techniques in medical devices, correct?
lines.style: Thoughtful, deliberate pacing. Slight pause before the question mark—like she's genuinely testing her memory or inviting him to clarify. Professional but genuinely interested.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、英国国教会の教区組織を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes, mine focused on parish organization in the Anglican Church.
lines.style: Even, measured response. No apology in the tone, just factual. Mild internal smile—aware of the odd specificity of his topic. Grounded and steady.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 昆虫の脱皮過程を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: So you researched the molting process in insects?
lines.style: Engaged and warm. Slight lift in tone—genuine interest, not performative. Leans in slightly. The curiosity of someone who finds each answer worth knowing.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、地質学の表層分析を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes, I focused on surface-layer analysis in geology.
lines.style: Direct, unadorned. The same steady rhythm as before. Small but genuine. Unapologetic about the technical specificity.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、大草原平原の生態研究を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Your research covered prairie ecosystems, then?
lines.style: Reflective, almost gentle questioning. Slower pace—she's working through something as she speaks. Not quite a statement, not quite a question. Thoughtful respect for his work.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、氷河の融解速度研究を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes, I studied glacial melting rates.
lines.style: Calm, final confirmation. Small fade at the end—a natural close to the exchange. Honest, complete. No elaboration needed.
